predecessors.name: Sultanate of Rum
predecessors.text: Kütahya and the Phrygian highlands, the western march of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: the Germiyan lands (Kütahya, Kula, Denizli, Karahisar and the Ankara country), bequeathed by Yakub II to Murad II and annexed in 1429

ledger.x: 1300: Yakub I founds the Germiyan beylik at Kütahya.
1333: Germiyan takes land round Eğirdir and Isparta from Hamid.
1344: Germiyan takes the remaining Hamid lands in Cliopatria (69 of 70 gained western cells lie in Hamid's last shape).
1363: Cliopatria extends Germiyan east to Ankara.
1381: Suleiman Shah gives Kütahya, Simav, Eğrigöz and Tavşanlı to the Ottomans as the dowry of his daughter Devletşah, who marries Bayezid.
1381: the court retreats from Kütahya to Kula.
1390: Bayezid I takes the whole of Germiyan.
1402: Timur's victory over the Ottomans restores Germiyan to Yakub II.
1410 (September): war breaks out between Germiyan and Karaman.
1411: Kütahya falls to Karaman and the fighting ends in a Karaman gain; no treaty is on the page.
1411: Mehmed II of Karaman takes Kütahya.
1429 (January): Yakub II dies and Murad II annexes Germiyan by his will.

wars.name: Catalan Company's campaign against Germiyan
wars.outcome: Philadelphia was lost to the Catalans in the spring of 1304; the page adds that Simav and Kula were 'later regained by the Catalan Company' and that Mehmed Chakhshadan 'retook Kula and Angir from the Catalan Company'.

wars.name: Ottoman absorption of Germiyan
wars.outcome: By the dowry marriage of 1381 the Ottomans gained Kütahya and its towns; 'In 1390, the entire realm of Germiyan came under Ottoman control'.

wars.name: Germiyan-Karaman war of 1410
wars.outcome: Karaman took Kütahya in 1411 and interrupted Yakub's reign; Mehmed Çelebi reinstated Yakub in 1414.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary for the Germiyan lands; frontiers with Karaman, Hamid, Aydin, Saruhan and the Ottomans are approximate throughout.
